llm.reply:
The genes associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome are cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A, checkpoint kinase 2, and tumor protein p53 [1][2][3][4]. The disease identifier is Li-Fraumeni syndrome [2].

## Associated Genes

A primary associated gene is NCBIGene:7157 [4]. Another associated entity is NCBIGene:11200 [3]. In addition, the condition is linked to NCBIGene:1029 [1].

## Disease Characteristics

Li-Fraumeni syndrome is an inherited condition with high penetrance [19: "autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance with high penetrance"]. Mutations in the TP53 gene impair p53 function and permit the emergence of multiple cancers [19: "TP53 gene mutations cause the loss of function of p53, leading to downstream events permissive for development of various malignancies"]. Patients experience a high cumulative lifetime risk of malignancy [19: "very high lifetime cumulative risk of developing multiple malignancies"].

## Clinical Heterogeneity

Affected individuals frequently demonstrate marked clinical heterogeneity [22: "Clinical variability is commonly seen in Li-Fraumeni syndrome"]. Phenotypic variation occurs even across individuals carrying identical pathogenic variants [22: "Phenotypic heterogeneity is present among different families affected by the same pathogenic variant"]. Component malignancies include soft tissue sarcomas and brain tumors [19: "component tumors include soft tissue sarcomas, osteosarcoma, premenopausal breast cancer, brain tumors, and adrenal cortical carcinomas"].

The genes associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome are cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A, checkpoint kinase 2, and tumor protein p53 [1][2][3][4]. The disease concept is documented under the MedGen title Li-Fraumeni syndrome [6]. It is also cataloged under the literature entity name Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [7].

## Clinical Characteristics

This condition is an inherited cancer predisposition syndrome characterized by high penetrance and an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern [19: "autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance with high penetrance"]. A publication entitled Li-Fraumeni Syndrome addresses the condition [5], with primary data indexed under publication pmid: 27617148 [9]. The syndrome frequently involves early-onset malignancies and component tumors across multiple organ systems [21: "appearance of tumors in multiple organs generally at an early age"]. The literature includes a dedicated overview entitled Li-Fraumeni syndrome [10], which is linked to publication pmid: 27622479 [12].

## Phenotypic Heterogeneity

Patients harboring germline mutations exhibit diverse tumor spectra and substantial phenotypic variation [22: "Phenotypic heterogeneity is present among different families affected by the same pathogenic variant in TP53 gene"]. Additional literature titled Li-Fraumeni Syndrome discusses these underlying aspects [13], documented under publication pmid: 30333936 [15]. A dedicated study explores this topic under the title Li-Fraumeni syndrome heterogeneity [16], associated with publication pmid: 31691207 [18].

## Clinical Studies

Clinical research includes the trial Clinical, Genetic, Behavioral, Laboratory and Epidemiologic Characterization of Individuals and Families at High Risk of Breast/Ovarian Cancer [8]. Metabolic mechanisms are investigated in Role of p53 Gene in Metabolism Regulation in Patients With Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [11]. Further clinical phenotypes are studied in Characterization of Patients With Uncommon Presentations and/or Uncommon Diseases Associated With the Cardiovascular System [14]. Other clinical protocols include Clinical and Genetic Studies of Li-Fraumeni Syndrome [17], as well as LIFSCREEN : Evaluation of Whole Body MRI for Early Detection of Cancers in Subjects With P53 Mutation (Li-Fraumeni Syndrome) [20].
